chemicals.name: Water
chemicals.description: Distilled water. The universal solvent. Used to dilute acids and bases - but ALWAYS add acid to water, never water to acid.

chemicals.name: Hydrochloric Acid
chemicals.description: A strong acid that fumes in air. Reacts with bases to form salt and water, and with metals to release hydrogen gas.

chemicals.name: Sodium Hydroxide
chemicals.description: A strong base, also called caustic soda. Dissolving it in water releases heat. Neutralises acids.

chemicals.name: Sulfuric Acid
chemicals.description: A dense, oily strong acid. Its heat of dilution is violent - adding water to concentrated sulfuric acid can make it boil and spit.

chemicals.name: Copper(II) Sulfate
chemicals.description: Bright blue crystalline powder. Reacts with sodium hydroxide to form a pale blue precipitate of copper hydroxide.

chemicals.name: Potassium Permanganate
chemicals.description: Deep purple crystalline powder, a strong oxidising agent. Its colour fades as it is reduced, which makes it a useful visual indicator.

chemicals.name: Ethanol
chemicals.description: A volatile, flammable alcohol. Burns with a pale blue flame. Keep away from open burners.

chemicals.name: Sodium Chloride
chemicals.description: Common table salt, a white crystalline powder. Dissolves readily in water to give a clear, neutral solution.

chemicals.name: Acetone
chemicals.description: A fast-evaporating solvent used to clean glassware. Highly flammable vapour.

chemicals.name: Dilute Sulfuric Acid
chemicals.description: Sulfuric acid diluted in water. Still corrosive, but far less aggressive than the concentrated form.

chemicals.name: Salt Water
chemicals.description: The neutral product of an acid-base reaction, or simply salt dissolved in water.

chemicals.name: Copper(II) Hydroxide
chemicals.description: A pale blue gelatinous precipitate. Formed when a base meets a copper salt solution.

chemicals.name: Reaction Mixture
chemicals.description: The unseparated product of a reaction — a mix of products and leftover reactants.

reactions.title: Water added to concentrated acid
reactions.explanation: The water flash-boiled at the acid's surface and spat concentrated acid onto the bench. Dilute by adding the ACID to the WATER, slowly.

warning.title: NEVER add water to concentrated acid!
warning.text: Dilution releases intense heat right at the surface. The water can flash-boil and spit concentrated acid out of the beaker and into your face. Correct procedure: add the ACID to the WATER, slowly, down the side of the vessel, while stirring.

result.note: Acid has splattered - the bench needs cleaning.

reactions.title: Correct dilution
reactions.explanation: The large water volume absorbed the heat of dilution safely — the acid is only warm to the touch. This is the correct order.

warning.title: Correct procedure: acid into water
warning.text: The large volume of water absorbs the heat of dilution safely. The mixture only becomes warm. This is always the right order when diluting a concentrated acid.

result.note: Safely diluted acid, warm to the touch.

reactions.title: Neutralisation
reactions.explanation: The acid and base cancelled each other out. HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O — a neutral salt solution, and the reaction is exothermic so the beaker feels warm.

warning.title: Neutralisation
warning.text: A strong acid plus a strong base gives a neutral salt solution and water: HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O. The reaction is exothermic, so the beaker feels warm.

reactions.title: Neutralisation
reactions.explanation: The base cancelled the acid: a neutral solution of sodium sulfate in water forms. Strong acid plus strong base releases a lot of heat — the beaker is hot.

reactions.title: Precipitation
reactions.explanation: CuSO4 + 2NaOH → Cu(OH)2↓ + Na2SO4. The insoluble pale blue copper(II) hydroxide dropped out of the blue solution as a solid.

warning.title: Precipitation
warning.text: Sodium hydroxide meets copper(II) sulfate and an insoluble pale blue solid, copper(II) hydroxide, drops out of the clear blue solution.

result.note: A pale blue precipitate has formed.

reactions.title: Oxidation of Ethanol
reactions.explanation: The purple permanganate oxidised the ethanol to ethanal and was itself reduced — the deep purple colour was discharged as the reaction warmed the mixture.

result.note: The purple colour has been discharged by oxidation.
result.name: Oxidised Ethanol

reactions.title: Salt dissolves
reactions.explanation: NaCl split into Na+ and Cl− ions in the water — a clear, neutral salt solution forms with no temperature change.

reactions.title: Ignition!
reactions.explanation: The oxidiser and the volatile solvent ignited on contact, leaving burnt residue in the flask.

warning.title: Oxidiser plus flammable solvent!
warning.text: A strong oxidising agent and a volatile flammable solvent can ignite on contact. Never store or mix oxidisers with solvents; keep them on separate shelves.

result.note: Burnt residue - use the fire extinguisher next time.
result.name: Burnt Residue

reactions.title: Chlorine gas!
reactions.explanation: The permanganate oxidised the chloride ions and released toxic green-yellow chlorine gas (Cl2). This must only be done in a fume hood.

warning.title: Toxic chlorine gas!
warning.text: Potassium permanganate oxidises concentrated hydrochloric acid and releases chlorine gas (Cl2) — a toxic, corrosive, green-yellow gas. This reaction must only ever be done in a fume hood.

result.note: Green-yellow chlorine gas has bubbled off; a pale manganese(II) chloride solution remains.
result.name: Manganese(II) Chloride Solution

reactions.title: Manganese heptoxide!
reactions.explanation: The concentrated acid dehydrated the permanganate into manganese heptoxide — a dark green oil that explodes on contact with almost anything. Never mix oxidisers with concentrated acids!

warning.title: Explosive compound formed!
warning.text: KMnO4 with concentrated H2SO4 forms manganese heptoxide (Mn2O7), a dark green oil that detonates above ~55°C or on contact with organic matter. This mixture must never be attempted.

result.note: A dangerously unstable green oil has formed - don't touch it.
result.name: Manganese Heptoxide Oil

reactions.title: Hydrogen chloride fumes!
reactions.explanation: The concentrated acid displaced HCl from the salt — acrid white fumes of hydrogen chloride rose off the mixture. This is the classic lab preparation of HCl gas.

warning.title: Corrosive acid fumes!
warning.text: Concentrated H2SO4 reacts with NaCl to give hydrogen chloride gas — the classic lab preparation. It forms stinging white fumes that are corrosive to the airways, so it must be done in a fume hood.

result.note: Fumes have cleared; sodium hydrogen sulfate remains.
result.name: Sodium Hydrogen Sulfate

reactions.title: Aldol condensation
reactions.explanation: The base pulled a hydrogen off an acetone molecule, joining two acetones into diacetone alcohol — the mixture slowly turns yellow-brown.

result.note: Diacetone alcohol has formed - the liquid is turning yellow.
result.name: Diacetone Alcohol

reactions.title: Acid dilutes
reactions.explanation: The acid simply dissolved into the water, becoming more dilute. Dissolving hydrogen chloride releases heat, so the liquid warms slightly.

reactions.title: Caustic soda dissolves
reactions.explanation: The caustic soda dissolved vigorously, giving off heat — the flask is warm to the touch. No reaction: a sodium hydroxide solution forms.

result.note: Sodium hydroxide solution, warm from dissolution.

reactions.title: Copper sulfate dissolves
reactions.explanation: The blue crystals dissolved into a deep blue solution — the copper(II) sulfate hydrate forms as the salt takes up water.

result.note: A deep blue copper sulfate solution.

reactions.title: Permanganate dissolves
reactions.explanation: The purple crystals dissolved into a deep purple solution — the permanganate ion colours the water intensely.

reactions.title: Ethanol mixes
reactions.explanation: Ethanol and water are completely miscible — no reaction, just one solution. The total volume shrinks slightly as the molecules pack together.

reactions.title: Acetone mixes
reactions.explanation: Acetone dissolves freely in water — the mixture cools a little as it mixes. No reaction.

reactions.title: Salt dissolves in acid
reactions.explanation: No reaction — the copper sulfate crystals just dissolved into the acid, giving a blue solution.

result.note: Copper sulfate dissolved in the acid.

reactions.title: Salt dissolves
reactions.explanation: No reaction — the solution already contains chloride ions, so the extra salt simply dissolves into it.

result.note: Extra salt dissolved into the chloride solution.

reactions.title: Two acids — no reaction
reactions.explanation: Both are acids; acids do not react with each other. The two liquids simply mixed.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Ethanol does not react with hydrochloric acid at room temperature — they simply mixed.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Acetone and hydrochloric acid do not react at room temperature — they mixed into a pale liquid.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Cold sodium hydroxide does not react with permanganate. (Heated together they would turn green as manganate forms.)

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide barely dissolves in ethanol and does not react with it at room temperature.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Sodium chloride and sodium hydroxide share the same cation — nothing reacts; the salt just sits in the base.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Copper sulfate is stable in sulfuric acid — no reaction; the powder simply mixed with the acid.

reactions.title: No reaction — for now
reactions.explanation: At room temperature the alcohol and acid only mix. Heated, the acid would dehydrate ethanol into ethene gas.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Acetone and sulfuric acid mix without reacting at room temperature.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: The blue sulfate and purple permanganate simply mixed — both salts stay as they are.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Copper sulfate does not dissolve in ethanol or react with it — the crystals settle at the bottom.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Two soluble salts with no reactive pair of ions — they simply mixed.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: The blue powder does not dissolve in acetone and does not react with it.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Sodium chloride does not reduce permanganate — the salt and the crystals simply mixed.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Salt does not dissolve in ethanol — the crystals sink and nothing reacts.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Both are flammable organic solvents — they mix completely without reacting.

reactions.title: No reaction
reactions.explanation: Salt is insoluble in acetone — the crystals just sink to the bottom.

reactions.title: More water
reactions.explanation: The flask now holds more of the same liquid — no reaction, just extra volume.

reactions.title: More acid
reactions.explanation: More hydrochloric acid was added — the acid simply got stronger in volume, no reaction.

reactions.title: More base
reactions.explanation: More sodium hydroxide was added — the base just got a bigger volume, no reaction.

reactions.title: More acid
reactions.explanation: More sulfuric acid was added — the acid just got a bigger volume, no reaction.

reactions.title: More crystals
reactions.explanation: More copper sulfate was added — the pile of blue crystals simply grew, no reaction.

reactions.title: More crystals
reactions.explanation: More permanganate was added — the pile of purple crystals simply grew, no reaction.

reactions.title: More ethanol
reactions.explanation: The flask now holds more of the same alcohol — no reaction, just extra volume.

reactions.title: More salt
reactions.explanation: More salt was added — the pile of white crystals simply grew, no reaction.

reactions.title: More acetone
reactions.explanation: The flask now holds more of the same solvent — no reaction, just extra volume.
